objects_domains_quantifiers: d is an integer with d>=2 and kappa is a real scalar with kappa>=2 for the actual S4.SS1 family; do not import main-theorem delta/d0/kappa<=d^(1-delta)/epsilon assumptions.
i ranges over source indices 1,...,d. For zero-based Fin d, theta_i must be ((i+1/2)*pi)/d, after real coercion; not ((i-1/2)*pi)/d.

O is any real square orthogonal matrix O^T O=I. Both determinant signs are included. No SO(d), det=+1, genericity, Haar-almost-sure or random-isotropy restriction is justified for the deterministic local results.
A=O Lambda O^T; A is symmetric, positive definite, invertible, and I<=A<=kappa I as conclusions/dependency facts, never convenience public assumptions on the fixed hard family.
The public potential is literally V_A=f_A:x in Euclidean R^d -> (1/2)*x^T A x on the whole space; x and y are arbitrary, not almost everywhere or in a bounded set.
C-infinity means all finite Frechet derivative orders with continuity on the whole Euclidean space. Hessian is the Euclidean x-Hessian, not derivative in O or A.
Hessian equality is pointwise for every x; as a bilinear form it sends (h,k) to <h,A k>, and as a Euclidean linear operator it is A. Representations need a reviewed adapter.
Gradient equals A x for every x. The exact first-order oracle is a map x -> (V_A(x),A x) into R x R^d with standard product Borel structure, for each fixed admissible source input.
Strong convexity constant is exactly the valid lower bound 1; smoothness constant exactly the valid upper bound kappa. They are uniform in O and x,y, with no unspecified d/O-dependent multiplier.
The unique minimizer is exactly 0 over all R^d: V_A(0)=0, V_A(x)>=||x||^2/2, and x!=0 implies V_A(x)>0.
Generalizations to d=1 or kappa>=1 may be true but must be identified as generalizations. In particular kappa=1 removes strict 1<lambda_i<kappa and cannot inherit that strict source proof.

expected_source_bridges.obligation: Discharge index/denominator/coercion positivity to prove 0<theta_i<pi from the actual source grid.
Use cosine strict range on (0,pi) and kappa-1>0 to obtain strict eigenvalue bounds.
Real diagonal Lambda is symmetric; conjugation A=O Lambda O^T is symmetric. Orthogonality on square matrices gives both O^T O=I and O O^T=I and preserves Euclidean norm.
For all z, ||z||^2<=z^T A z<=kappa||z||^2; transport diagonal sums through O^T and interpret this as Loewner inequalities.
The literal finite-dimensional quadratic is C-infinity. This branch needs the formula, not a random-input event or full spectral admissibility.

Differentiate the literal symmetric quadratic to get DV_A(x)[h]=<A x,h>, gradient A x, and D2 V_A(x)[h,k]=<h,A k> independent of x. Symmetry is essential to identifying Hessian as A rather than its symmetric part.
Lower Hessian/quadratic bound implies V_A(y)>=V_A(x)+<A x,y-x>+(1/2)||y-x||^2. Verify convention/factor when using a convexity predicate.

Upper spectral bound implies ||A(x-y)||<=kappa||x-y|| in Euclidean induced operator norm; hence gradient is globally kappa-Lipschitz. Do not substitute function Lipschitzness or an entrywise/Frobenius matrix norm.

Evaluate V_A(0); use lower quadratic bound and positivity of Euclidean norm squared off zero to derive strict positivity and unique global minimizer, with no pre-given minimizer/existence/coercivity binder.

For fixed source input, actual potential is continuous (polynomial), A x is continuous (linear), and their pair is continuous/Borel. Measurability belongs to the actual oracle, not a surrogate map or arbitrary supplied oracle.
Identify f_A and V_A by their identical literal formula and identify matrix-coordinate representations with the standard Euclidean vector/inner-product structure.

definition_challenge: The hard grid, diagonal, conjugated precision, potential and exact oracle are literal definitions. Audit complete meaning-carrying bodies and all parameter/default branches on the public carrier.

The source does not define an arbitrary admissible potential then choose one. Substituting a characterized potential, a cutoff, shifted potential, clipped spectrum, surrogate oracle, or fallback zero changes the object.
V_A and f_A differ only in notation here. A formal additive shift could preserve derivative geometry but changes the exact source value oracle and V_A(0)=0.

If a minimizer object is introduced by choice, actual existence/uniqueness must be proved before characterization; no if-exists/otherwise-default definition is justified.
Hessian-as-matrix, Hessian-as-bilinear-form, and derivative-as-continuous-linear-map require explicit semantic equivalence, including Euclidean inner product and norm conventions.
